summary:
[  edit  ]
The GLSL  TOP  renders a GLSL  shader  into a  TOP  image. Use the Info  DAT  to check for compile errors in your shaders.
The GLSL  TOP  can act as a pixel shader, or the more general and complex  Compute Shader . Caveat: Compute Shaders need GLSL 4.30 or later.
The GLSL  TOP  has one docked compute shader as well as a normal GLSL shader. Change he Mode to Compute  Shader . it will use the  glsl1_compute   DAT .
Refer to the  Write a GLSL TOP  article for more info on using this  TOP .
See the  GLSL Category  for more information, and  Compute Shader .

parameters.label: GLSL Version
parameters.name: glslversion
parameters.description: ⊞  - Pick what version of GLSL to compile the shader with.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Choose what type of shader you are writing, vertex/pixel shader, or a compute shader.

parameters.label: Preprocess Directives
parameters.name: predat
parameters.description: Use this  DAT  to place preprocessor directives at the start of your shader, such as #extension. This is required since these need to be the first lines in the shader, and TouchDesigner will be adding code to the start of your shader to declare uniforms/functions which would appear before #extension directives located in the main shader. #include statements should be avoided unless include-guards are in the DATs. This should  not  be used for pre-prending common code to your shaders. Use #include statements in the main shader to do that.

parameters.label: Vertex   Shader
parameters.name: vertexdat
parameters.description: Points to the  DAT  holding the  Vertex   Shader . Drag & Drop a  DAT  here, or manually enter the path to the  DAT .

parameters.label: Pixel  Shader
parameters.name: pixeldat
parameters.description: Points to the  DAT  holding the Pixel  Shader . Drag & Drop a  DAT  here, or manually enter the path to the  DAT .

parameters.label: Compute  Shader
parameters.name: computedat
parameters.description: Points to the  DAT  holding the  Compute Shader . Drag & Drop a  DAT  here, or manually enter the path to the  DAT .

parameters.label: Load Uniform Names
parameters.name: loaduniformnames
parameters.description: When this button is pressed the node will try to pre-fill all it's uniform parameter with uniforms that are declare in the shader. Note that the shader compiler will likely not expose uniforms that are unused.

parameters.label: Dispatch Size
parameters.name: dispatchsize
parameters.description: ⊞  - The dispatch size to use when executing a compute shader.

parameters.label: Output Access
parameters.name: outputaccess
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls how the output textures will be accessed. If the textures will be read from (such as using previous frame's values), then the access should be changed to Read-Write instead of Write Only.

parameters.label: Write Only
parameters.name: writeonly
parameters.description: The texture will only be written to by the shader, not read.

parameters.label: Read-Write
parameters.name: readwrite
parameters.description: The texture will be both written and read by the shader.

parameters.label: Output Type
parameters.name: type
parameters.description: ⊞  - Specify what type of texture to create. When creating  a 3D texture the  TOP  will render once for every slice of the output. Refer to   3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays  for more info.

parameters.label: 2D Texture
parameters.name: texture2d
parameters.description: Creates a 2D texture.

parameters.label: 2D Texture Array
parameters.name: texture2darray
parameters.description: Creates a  2D Texture Array . Slices of the array can be access using a non-normalized integer index for the w coordinate.

parameters.label: 3D Texture
parameters.name: texture3d
parameters.description: Creates a  3D Texture . Slices of the array can be accessed using the w coordinate in the range 0-1. Value of the texture in between slices are interpolated.

parameters.label: Depth
parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: ⊞  - Set the depth of the 3D texture from the  Input  or the  Custom Depth  parameter.

parameters.label: Custom Depth
parameters.name: customdepth
parameters.description: Manually set the depth of the 3D texture, otherwise it will use the depth of the input.

parameters.label: Auto Dispatch Size
parameters.name: autodispatchsize
parameters.description: Automatically set the dispatch size based on the compute shader's local size and the output texture resolution. Ensures at least one thread per pixel will execute.

parameters.label: Clear Outputs
parameters.name: clearoutputs
parameters.description: When using a Compute  Shader , this controls if the output texture should be cleared at the start of each cook. Otherwise the data from the previous cook will stay in the texture, and pixels can be left as-is in the Compute  Shader .

parameters.label: Clear Value
parameters.name: clearvalue
parameters.description: ⊞  - The color value to clear all pixels to at the start of the cook.

parameters.label: Input Mapping
parameters.name: inputmapping
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines how the node's input(s) are passed into the shader for use when creating a 3D Texture. By default all of the inputs are passed to each slice. When using the  N inputs per Slice  mode, the first N inputs are passed to the first slice, the next N inputs are passed the second slice, and so on. When it runs out of inputs it loops back to the first input. N is selected by the parameter  N Value .

parameters.label: N Value
parameters.name: nval
parameters.description: Determines how many inputs are passed to the shader per slice when using the  N inputs per Slice  mode for  Input Mapping . If for example this is set to 2, then the first 2 inputs will be passed to the first slice, the next 2 inputs will be passed the second slice, and so on. It will loop back to the start of the inputs if it runs out before it reaches the last slice.

parameters.label: Input Extend Mode UV
parameters.name: inputextenduv
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls what is returned from your texture sampling functions when the U and V texture coordinates (called S and T in the shader) are outside [0-1] range.

parameters.label: Input Extend Mode W
parameters.name: inputextendw
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls what is returned from your texture sampling functions when the W texture coordinate (called W in the shader) are outside [0-1] range. Only useful for  3D Texture .

parameters.label: # of Color Buffers
parameters.name: numcolorbufs
parameters.description: Any shader you write can output to more than one RGBA buffer at a time. Turn up this value to have more color buffers allocated for you, and refer to [Write_a_GLSL_ TOP #Outputting_to_Multiple_Color_Buffers Write a GLSL  TOP ] for more information on using this feature.

parameters.label: TDSimplexNoise()
parameters.name: simplexnoise
parameters.description: ⊞  - Pick between Performance vs Quality Simplex noise. Performance mode picks the existing TDSimplexNoise(). Quality noise reduces certain artifacts and axis alignment issues with the existing simplex noise at the cost of speed.

parameters.label: Performance
parameters.name: performance
parameters.description: Performant noise.

parameters.label: Quality
parameters.name: quality
parameters.description: Quality noise.

parameters.label: Pre-Multiply RGB by Alpha
parameters.name: premultrgbbyalpha
parameters.description: Multiplies the RGB values in all the Color parameters by their Alpha value, before passing them to the shader.

parameters.label: Name
parameters.name: color0name
parameters.description: The name of the uniform in the shader to assign this color value to.

parameters.label: RGB
parameters.name: color0rgb
parameters.description: ⊞  - The RGB values for this uniform.

parameters.label: Alpha
parameters.name: color0alpha
parameters.description: The Alpha value for this uniform.

parameters.label: Vector
parameters.name: vec
parameters.description: Sequence of vector uniforms

parameters.label: Name
parameters.name: vec0name
parameters.description: The uniform name, as declared in the shader

parameters.label: Value
parameters.name: vec0value
parameters.description: ⊞  - The value(s) to give the uniform.

parameters.label: CHOP  Uniforms allow you to send  CHOP  channel data into a GLSL shader as an array. Depending on the array type used, the number of values you can send into the shader may be limited. If you are using Uniform Arrays, you can use the Built
parameters.description: In variable  int(var('SYS_GFX_GLSL_MAX_UNIFORMS'))  to get an idea of how many values you can pass to the shader. Current GPUs are vec4 based for uniform arrays, so the maximum array size is  int(var('SYS_GFX_GLSL_MAX_UNIFORMS')) / 4 . Other uniforms will take away from this maximum. If you are using Texture Buffers the maximum array size is far bigger,  int(var('SYS_GFX_MAX_TEXTURE_BUFFER_SIZE'))  will tell you the max for this. The max for texture buffer is per texture buffer, and having multiple texture buffers does not take away from the max for each array.

parameters.label: Array
parameters.name: array
parameters.description: Sequence of array uniforms

parameters.label: Name
parameters.name: array0name
parameters.description: The name of the uniform. You can send up to 4 channels into the GLSL shader in a single uniform. The number of channels is determined by the float/vec2/vec3/vec4 menu to the right of the name. For a  CHOP  with a single channel declare your uniform as a float, for one with two channels declare your uniform as a vec2, etc. The data is interleaved in the uniform. I.e the .x component is the 1st channel, .y is the 2nd channel, etc.

parameters.label: Type
parameters.name: array0type
parameters.description: ⊞  - The data type of the uniform in the shader.

parameters.label: CHOP
parameters.name: array0chop
parameters.description: The channels from this  CHOP  will be sent to the GLSL shader.

parameters.label: Array Type
parameters.name: array0arraytype
parameters.description: ⊞  - The type of the uniform.

parameters.label: Uniform Array
parameters.name: uniformarray
parameters.description: All GPUs can send array data into a GLSL shader using Uniform Arrays.

parameters.label: Texture Buffer
parameters.name: texturebuffer
parameters.description: Newer GPUs can send array data into a GLSL shader using Texture Buffers. Texture Buffers use texture memory and texture fetches to access the data, which allows them to store many more values.

parameters.label: Where i is the 0
parameters.description: based index (an integer) into the buffer that you want to get a value for.

parameters.label: Matrix
parameters.name: matrix
parameters.description: Sequence of matrix uniforms

parameters.label: Name
parameters.name: matrix0name
parameters.description: The name of the matrix uniform.

parameters.label: Matrix
parameters.name: matrix0value
parameters.description: The value to assign the matrix. For valid ways to specify this, see the  Matrix Parameters  article.

parameters.label: Atomic Counter
parameters.name: ac
parameters.description: Sequence of atomic counter uniforms

parameters.label: Name
parameters.name: ac0name
parameters.description: The name of the uniform.

parameters.label: Initial Value Type
parameters.name: ac0initvalue
parameters.description: ⊞  - Specifies how the atomic counters receive their initial value, either through a single default value or a  CHOP .

parameters.label: Initial Value
parameters.name: ac0singlevalue
parameters.description: Specifies a single value that all atomic counters in this binding will be initialized to.

parameters.label: Initial Values  CHOP
parameters.name: ac0chopvalue
parameters.description: A reference to the  CHOP  that will determine the initial values of the atomic counters in this binding. The  CHOP  will be spanned in track order, so the values from the first track will be read in order first, then the next track (if there is one) and so on. If there are more initial values to fill than there are values in the  CHOP  then they will all be set to 0. Atomic counters will be initialized from low to high offsets.

parameters.label: Constant
parameters.name: const
parameters.description: Sequence of constant uniforms

parameters.label: Name
parameters.name: const0name
parameters.description: The constant name, as declared in the shader.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.name: const0value
parameters.description: The value to give the constant.

parameters.label: POP
parameters.name: buffer0pop
parameters.description: The path to the  POP  to get the attribute buffer from.

parameters.label: Attribute Class
parameters.name: buffer0attrclass
parameters.description: ⊞  - The class of the attribute that is being referenced

parameters.label: Attribute
parameters.name: buffer0attr
parameters.description: The name of the attribute in the  POP .

parameters.label: Name
parameters.name: buffer0name
parameters.description: The name you want to reference this attribute by inside the shader.

parameters.label: Output  Resolution
parameters.name: outputresolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - quickly change the resolution of the  TOP 's data.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's resolution.

parameters.label: Eighth
parameters.name: eighth
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Quarter
parameters.name: quarter
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Half
parameters.name: half
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 2X
parameters.name: 2x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 4X
parameters.name: 4x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 8X
parameters.name: 8x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Fit  Resolution
parameters.name: fit
parameters.description: Fits the width and height to the resolution given below, while maintaining the aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Limit  Resolution
parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The width and height are limited to the resolution given below. If one of the dimensions exceeds the given resolution, the width and height will be reduced to fit inside the given limits while maintaining the aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Custom  Resolution
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Enables the  Resolution  parameter below, giving direct control over width and height.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enabled only when the  Resolution  parameter is set to Custom  Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.name: resmenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.name: resmult
parameters.description: Uses the Global  Resolution  Multiplier found in  Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global  Resolution  Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this  TOP  is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Uses the aspect of the image's defined resolution (ie 512x256 would be 2:1), whereby each pixel is square.

parameters.label: Custom Aspect
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Lets you explicitly define a custom aspect ratio in the Aspect parameter below.

parameters.label: Aspect
parameters.name: aspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Use when Output Aspect parameter is set to Custom Aspect.

parameters.label: Aspect Menu
parameters.name: armenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used aspect ratios.

parameters.label: Input Smoothness
parameters.name: inputfiltertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering on the input image of the  TOP .

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. This is how you get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.label: Fill  Viewer
parameters.name: fillmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determine how the  TOP  image is displayed in the viewer.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the same Fill Viewer settings as it's input.

parameters.label: Fill
parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: Stretches the image to fit the edges of the viewer.

parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer horizontally.

parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer vertically.

parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.name: best
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so no part of image is cropped.

parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.name: outside
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so image fills viewer while constraining it's proportions. This often leads to part of image getting cropped by viewer.

parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.description: Displays the native resolution of the image in the viewer.

parameters.label: Viewer Smoothness
parameters.name: filtertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering in the viewers.

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. Use this to get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.label: Passes
parameters.name: npasses
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the  TOP  the specified number of times. Making this larger than 1 is essentially the same as taking the output from each pass, and passing it into the first input of the node and repeating the process. Other inputs and parameters remain the same for each pass.

parameters.label: Channel Mask
parameters.name: chanmask
parameters.description: Allows you to choose which channels (R, G, B, or A) the  TOP  will operate on. All channels are selected by default.

parameters.label: Pixel Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - Format used to store data for each channel in the image (ie. R, G, B, and A). Refer to  Pixel Formats  for more information.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's pixel format.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel.

parameters.label: sRGB 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: srgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel and stores color in sRGB colorspace.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16float
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba32float
parameters.description: Uses 32-bits per color channel, 128-bits per pixels.

parameters.label: 10-bit RGB, 2-bit Alpha, fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgb10a2fixed
parameters.description: Uses 10-bits per color channel and 2-bits for alpha, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16fixed
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 11-bit float (RGB), Positive Values Only
parameters.name: rgba11float
parameters.description: A RGB floating point format that has 11 bits for the Red and Green channels, and 10-bits for the Blue  Channel , 32-bits total per pixel (therefore the same memory usage as 8-bit RGBA). The Alpha channel in this format will always be 1. Values can go above one, but can't be negative. ie. the range is [0, infinite).

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.name: mono8fixed
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.name: mono16fixed
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono)
parameters.name: mono16float
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (Mono)
parameters.name: mono32float
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RG)
parameters.name: rg8fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 8-bits per channel, 16-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RG)
parameters.name: rg16fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (RG)
parameters.name: rg16float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (RG)
parameters.name: rg32float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 32-bits per channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (A)
parameters.name: a8fixed
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 8-bits per channel, 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (A)
parameters.name: a16fixed
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 16-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (A)
parameters.name: a16float
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 16-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (A)
parameters.name: a32float
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 32-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha8fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 8-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha16fixed
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha16float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.name: monoalpha32float
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 32-bits per channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: Parameter Color Space
parameters.name: parmcolorspace
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls how all color parameters on this node are interpreted. The color values as treated as being in the selected color space, and are converted to the Working  Color Space  before they are used as part of the node's operation. Note that this does not change the color space of the node itself, as that is always in the Working Color Space.

parameters.label: sRGB
parameters.name: srgb
parameters.description: sRGB  color space, with sRGB transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: sRGB - Linear
parameters.name: srgblinear
parameters.description: sRGB  color space, with linear transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Rec.601 (NTSC)
parameters.name: rec601ntsc
parameters.description: Rec.601  with NTSC primaries color space, with Rec.601 transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Rec.709
parameters.name: rec709
parameters.description: Rec.709  color space, with Rec.709 (same as Rec.2020) transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Rec.2020
parameters.name: rec2020
parameters.description: Rec.2020  color space, with Rec.2020 (same as Rec.709) transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: DCI-P3
parameters.name: dcip3
parameters.description: DCI-P3  color space, with D65 white point and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: DCI-P3 (D60)
parameters.name: dcip3d60
parameters.description: DCI-P3 "D60 sim"  color space, with D60 white point, and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Display-P3 (D65)
parameters.name: displayp3d65
parameters.description: Display-P3  color space, with D65 white point, and sRGB gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: ACES2065-1
parameters.name: aces2065
parameters.description: 1  -  ACES 2065-1  (also known as ACES AP0) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: ACEScg
parameters.name: acescg
parameters.description: ACEScg  (also known as ACES AP1) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Passthrough
parameters.name: passthrough
parameters.description: When selected, the color values will be used as-is in the operation, without any modification or attempt to convert them into the Working Color Space.

parameters.label: Parameter Reference  White
parameters.name: parmreferencewhite
parameters.description: ⊞  - When converting a parameter color value to the Working Color Space, this controls how it should be treated with respect to  Reference White . If the Working Color Space is the same  Reference  White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the  Reference  White level (brightness) of this color will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR  Reference  White of 120 nits, and the HDR  Reference  White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

parameters.label: Default For Color Space
parameters.name: default
parameters.description: Will use either the SDR or the HDR  Reference  White, based on the color space selected.

parameters.label: Use Parent  Panel
parameters.name: useparent
parameters.description: Will use the  Reference  White that the parent panel has selected. If the top-level panel also has 'Use  Parent ' selected, then 'UI  Reference  White' will be used.

parameters.label: Standard (SDR)
parameters.name: sdr
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as SDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.label: High (HDR)
parameters.name: hdr
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as HDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.label: UI
parameters.name: ui
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as UI for it's reference white value. This uses the 'UI  Reference  White Nits' value for it's brightness.

parameters.label: Parameter Color Space
parameters.name: parmcolorspace
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls how all color parameters on this node are interpreted. The color values as treated as being in the selected color space, and are converted to the Working  Color Space  before they are used as part of the node's operation. Note that this does not change the color space of the node itself, as that is always in the Working Color Space.

parameters.label: sRGB
parameters.name: srgb
parameters.description: sRGB  color space, with sRGB transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: sRGB - Linear
parameters.name: srgblinear
